card.statement:
The Whittaker vector $v_{G}$ of the deformed Virasoro algebra exists uniquely, and in the bosonized form it is given by $v_{G}=\sum_{n\geq 0}L^{n}v_{G,n}$ with

$\displaystyle v_{G,n}=\sum_{\lambda\,\vdash n}P_{\lambda}(q,t)\gamma_{\lambda},\quad\gamma_{\lambda}=\prod_{s\in\lambda}\dfrac{k}{1-k^{2}q^{j(s)}t^{-i(s)}}\dfrac{q^{a_{\lambda}(s)}}{1-q^{1+a_{\lambda}(s)}t^{l_{\lambda}(s)}}$

(1.6)

2. Preliminary

The purpose of this subsection is a rewriting of the Whittaker condition in terms of the key objects $\eta(z)$ and $D(z)$. These are Laurent formal series of operators acting on the Fock space, and part of the generating currents of the Ding-Iohara-Miki algebra. $\eta(z)$ has another feature related to Macdonald symmetric functions: The zero-th mode $\eta_{0}$ realizes the first-order Macdonald difference operator. The importance of this current have been observed in the past studies [SKAO, S06, FHHSY, FFJMM].

2.1. Rewriting in the integral form

First we rewrite the Whittaker vector (1.6) in terms of the integral form of Macdonald symmetric functions. For that purpose, we shall prepare several combinatorial notations.

For a partition $\lambda=(\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2},\ldots)$ we use the common symbol

$n(\lambda):=\sum_{i}(i-1)\lambda_{i}.$

One can immediately see that

$\displaystyle n(\lambda)=\sum_{s\in\lambda}(i(s)-1),\quad n(\lambda^{\prime})=\sum_{s\in\lambda}(j(s)-1).$

(2.1)

Here the running index $s\in\lambda$ means that $s$ runs over the set of boxes in the Young diagram (associated to) $\lambda$. The symbols $i(s)$ and $j(s)$ are the coordinates of the box $s$. As explained in NOTATION, we have $1\leq i(s)\leq\ell(\lambda)$ and $1\leq j(s)\leq\lambda_{i(s)}$ for any $s\in\lambda$.

Then the relationship between $P_{\lambda}(q,t)$ and $J_{\lambda}(q,t)$ is

$\displaystyle J_{\lambda}(q,t)=c_{\lambda}(q,t)P_{\lambda}(q,t)=c^{\prime}_{\lambda}(q,t)Q_{\lambda}(q,t).$

(2.2)

(See [M95, Chap VI., §8] for the detail.) Here the symmetric function $Q_{\lambda}(q,t)$ is the dual of $P_{\lambda}(q,t)$ with respect to the Macdonald inner product $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{q,t}$ on $\Lambda_{\mathbb{F}}$ defined by

$\displaystyle\langle p_{\lambda},p_{\mu}\rangle_{q,t}:=\delta_{\lambda,\mu}z_{\lambda}\prod_{i=1}^{\ell{\lambda}}\dfrac{1-q^{\lambda_{i}}}{1-t^{\lambda_{i}}}.$

(2.3)

The coefficients $c_{\lambda}(q,t)$ and $c^{\prime}_{\lambda}(q,t)$ are given by the product formula

$\displaystyle c_{\lambda}(s;q,t):=1-q^{a_{\lambda}(s)}t^{l_{\lambda}(s)+1},\qquad c^{\prime}_{\lambda}(s;q,t):=1-q^{a_{\lambda}(s)+1}t^{l_{\lambda}(s)},\qquad$

(2.4)

$\displaystyle c_{\lambda}(q,t):=\prod_{s\in\lambda}c_{\lambda}(s;q,t),\qquad c^{\prime}_{\lambda}(q,t):=\prod_{s\in\lambda}c^{\prime}_{\lambda}(s;q,t).$

(2.5)

We also have

$\displaystyle\langle J_{\lambda}(q,t),J_{\mu}(q,t)\rangle_{q,t}=c_{\lambda}(q,t)c^{\prime}_{\lambda}(q,t)\delta_{\lambda,\mu}$

We also use the plethystic notation for symmetric functions. For an alphabet $X=(x_{1},x_{2},\ldots)$, a symmetric function with variables $X$ is denoted by $f[X]$. So, for example, the power symmetric function in the variables $X$ is denoted by $p_{n}[X]:=x_{1}^{n}+x_{2}^{n}+\cdots$.

We shall denote by

$\displaystyle H[X;u]:=\prod_{i}(1-uX_{i})^{-1}=\sum_{r\geq 0}u^{r}h_{r}[X]$

the generating function of the complete symmetric polynomials $h_{r}$ in the alphabet $X$.

Following the ideas in [BGHT], for each partition $\lambda$ we introduce the set

$\displaystyle B_{\lambda}:=\bigl\{q^{j-1}t^{1-i}\mid 1\leq i\leq\ell(\lambda),\,1\leq j\leq\lambda_{i}\bigr\}=\bigl\{q^{j(s)-1}t^{1-i(s)}\mid s\in\lambda\bigr\}.$

(2.6)

We shall use $B_{\lambda}$ as an alphabet of symmetric polynomials. For example, we have

$\displaystyle e_{1}[B_{\lambda}]=\sum_{s\in\lambda}q^{j(s)-1}t^{1-i(s)}.$

Now using (2.1), (2.2) and (2.6), we can rewrite the conjectural Whittaker vector formula (1.6) as follows:
card.label: Theorem 1.1

paper.title: Whittaker vector of deformed Virasoro algebra and Macdonald symmetric functions
paper.abstract: We give a proof of Awata and Yamada's conjecture for the explicit formula of Whittaker vector of the deformed Virasoro algebra realized in the Fock space. The formula is expressed as a summation over Macdonald symmetric functions with factored coefficients. In the proof we fully use currents appearing in the Fock representation of Ding-Iohara-Miki quantum algebra. We also mention an interpretation of Whittaker vector in terms of the geometry of the Hilbert schemes of points on the affine plane.
